summary: This topic provides a method for troubleshooting when variables are not printing correctly on a PDF template by using the browser's developer console to inspect the available data object and identify the correct variable names.
navigation: During template preview or printing: Right-click on the page > Inspect > Console tab
steps: Generate a preview or print the template that has missing variable data.
Right-click on the page and select 'Inspect' (or 'Inspect Element').
Navigate to the 'Console' tab in the developer tools.
Look for the object that contains the data (often named 'DisplayData' or similar).
Expand the object to view all available variables and their exact names (e.g., 'Category' vs. 'StudentCategory' vs. 'Student's category').
Compare the variable name found in the console with the variable name used in your template code.
Correct any discrepancies in the template code (e.g., change 'DisplayData.Student's category' to 'DisplayData.Category').
Reprint or preview the template to verify the fix.
business_rules: Variables must exactly match the names provided in the data object found in the console.
The 'DisplayData.' prefix is mandatory for calling values from the data array.
important_notes: A common issue is using a slightly different variable name in the template code than what is actually available in the data object.
The console will show all data passed to the template, including student details, fee information, institute details, etc.
Arrays within objects (e.g., for fee heads, installments) require loops to display, which is a more advanced topic.
